From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Runtime & deletion questions for prospective deployment

Hi Anna — thanks, and glad the demo was useful. High-level answers up front, and I attached a short one-page summary for procurement: redwood-residency-compact.pdf.

- Hosted (Redwood API): Requests are routed to a regional control plane and executed on compute in the closest compatible region. For EU customers we by default execute inference in EU regional pools (Frankfurt, Amsterdam, Paris) unless a different region is requested.
- Dedicated: Dedicated capacity is deployed into customer-selected regions; customers pick the region(s) and we provision GPU pools there (on prem or cloud).
- Subprocessors: Primary cloud footprint uses our EU cloud provider partners (compute, object storage), a CDN provider (EU POPs), and a limited monitoring/log aggregation vendor. We keep an up-to-date subprocessor list; I attached the current inventory. No non-EU subprocessors touch inference payloads for EU-region tenants under our default configuration.
- Deletion timeline: For record-level erase requests we remove customer data from active runtime caches within minutes and from persistent object stores within 24–72 hours depending on backlog and retention windows. Complete eradication from backups is an additional process that can take up to 30 days; we provide a written attestation on request.

If helpful I can loop in Monica (privacy ops) and Jordan (infra) to provide the audit log excerpts and the subprocessor roster. Do you want a short call early next week?

Thanks,
Rafael
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-residency-compact.pdf (1 page summary)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 11 Jul 2025 11:04:00 +02:00

Rafael / Jordan — see notes below (will attach full CSV and vendor statements in the drive link):

- Default EU hosting regions: eu-central-1 (Frankfurt), eu-west-1 (Ireland), eu-west-3 (Paris). We prefer eu-central-1 for low-latency FR/NL customers.
- Subprocessor roster (EU impact):
  • EU Cloud Provider A (compute + object storage) — Germany (EU data centers)
  • EU CDN Partner B — POPs across EU (no US routing for EU-tenants)
  • Monitoring vendor C — EU-only cluster (logs forwarded to EU region)
  • KMS/Keywrap provider D — EU HSM instances (customer keys optional)
- Non-EU subprocessors: only global analytics (aggregated telemetry) are processed in the US but telemetry is stripped of payloads; inference payloads remain in EU.
- Deletion timelines:
  • Runtime caches: minutes
  • Persistent stores (object): 24–72 hours
  • Backup destruction: up to 30 days
  • Audit log extracts: available on request; redaction performed to remove customer PII.

I'll upload the subprocessor CSV + vendor SOC pointers to the drive link and grant Lund Health read-only access. Good to include the attestation paragraph about no cross-border transfer for inference payloads under EU tenancy by default.

—Monica

Hi Anna — following up with the evidence pack and concise answers. See attached: redwood-residency-compact.pdf and llm-processing-arch.png. Key points:

1) Where requests execute
- Hosted API (EU tenancy): inference is executed in EU regional pools (default locations: Frankfurt, Ireland, Paris). We do not route inference payloads to non-EU subprocessors under this tenancy.
- Dedicated: capacity is provisioned to the customer-selected region; if you request on-prem or a specific EU cloud region we will deploy there.

2) Subprocessors that may touch payload metadata
- EU Cloud Provider A (compute & object storage) — Germany
- EU CDN Partner B — EU POPs
- Monitoring vendor C — EU cluster (logs are masked)
- KMS provider D — EU HSM instances (if enabled)
We have provided the full subprocessor CSV to the shared drive link (read-only).

3) Cross-border transfers
- Default behavior for EU-tenancy customers: inference payloads remain within EU regions; no cross-border export of raw payloads. Aggregated telemetry (no payloads) may be used in support pipelines and can be processed outside the EU for analytics; customers can opt out.

4) Deletion timeline
- Active runtime caches: minutes
- Persistent object stores: 24–72 hours
- Backups & long-term snapshots: up to 30 days for full purge; we can supply an attestation upon completion.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute call to walk procurement/security through the attachments and the sample audit logs (redacted). Are you available Wed 16 Jul between 08:00–11:00 CEST?

Regards,
Rafael
